item.title: Dutch suicide prevention website shares data with tech companies without consent
item.description:
📝 The Dutch suicide prevention hotline 113 shared data from website visitors with third parties without consent, BNR reports based on research by ethical hacker Mick Beer of Hackedemia. ”Stichting 113 likely violated the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) by sharing this data. ”Stichting 113 has temporarily disabled all measurement and analysis tools so that it no longer shares this data with third parties.
🔗 Read more: https://nltimes.nl/2026/05/13/dutch-suicide-prevention-hotline-shares-visitor-data-tech-companies

item.title: Using OR-Tools CP-SAT for Scheduling Problems
item.description:
📝 The process of evacuating multiple hosts for maintenance involves a complex scheduling problem with several constraints. With these challenges in mind, the goal of the scheduling problem is to find a schedule for the maintenance tasks that minimizes the total time to complete all maintenance while respecting these constraints. Maintenance scheduling in the cloud is close to a Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (RCPSP) without the precedence constraints.
🔗 Read more: https://atalaykutlay.com/or-tools-cp-sat-for-scheduling-problems.html

item.title: Software Developers Say AI Is Rotting Their Brains
item.description:
📝 Tech company executives are confident that AI will completely transform the economy and point to the changes they see in-house to prove that this change is coming fast. More concerning, developers who use AI at work report that they feel like they are de-skilling themselves and losing their ability to do their jobs as well as they used to. Tech company executives love to brag about how much of the code at their company is AI-generated.
🔗 Read more: https://www.404media.co/software-developers-say-ai-is-rotting-their-brains/

item.title: Cost of enum-to-string: C++26 reflection vs. the old ways
item.description:
📝 enchantum (c++17) A C++17 header-only library by ZXShady that achieves enum reflection through __PRETTY_FUNCTION__ parsing tricks. No macros at the call site, no reflection flag needed: #include <enchantum/enchantum. For example, the reflection variant for N=4 looks like this: #include "enum_to_string.
🔗 Read more: https://vittorioromeo.com/index/blog/refl_enum_to_string.html
